title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to their Driver Control Assistance System (DCAS), version 1.1.0
scope_summary: UN R171 approves vehicle types with regard to their Driver Control Assistance System (DCAS). A DCAS is an SAE level 2 system that gives sustained combined lateral and longitudinal motion-control support while the driver stays responsible, and the regulation covers motor vehicles of categories M and N (scope paragraph not reproduced in the supplied excerpt).
scope_quote: This UN Regulation addresses the Driver Control Assistance Systems (DCAS), which are a subset of ADAS. DCAS are driver-operated vehicle systems assisting a human driver in performing vehicle dynamic control via sustained lateral and longitudinal motion-control support. ... this UN Regulation intends to establish technologically neutral uniform and general provisions concerning the approval of vehicles equipped with DCAS that may function beyond the limitations imposed by the 03 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79
applies_to_components: Driver Control Assistance System (DCAS) as a whole (hardware and software)
DCAS features (e.g. lane keeping / positioning in lane, lane change, other manoeuvres)
environment perception / detection capability (sensors) of the DCAS
driver monitoring / driver engagement and availability detection
Human-Machine Interface (HMI): activation, deactivation, override, status indication, warnings
system failure detection and safety response
in-service monitoring and reporting of DCAS operation
electronic control system safety concept and documentation
simulation/virtual testing toolchain used for compliance evidence
relation_to_other_regulations: Allows approval of DCAS functioning beyond the limitations of the 03 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79 (steering equipment / ACSF); it fills a regulatory gap and does not formally replace R79.

Paragraph 5.2 regulates interaction with other vehicle assistance systems; based on general knowledge, these likely include systems under R79 (LKA/ESF/ACSF), R152 (AEBS) and R131 (AEBS heavy vehicles).
The communication form (Annex 1) references cyber security and software updates; based on general knowledge, these correspond to UN R155 and UN R156.
Annex 3 sets special requirements for the safety aspects of electronic control systems, analogous to the complex electronic systems annexes of other UN Regulations (e.g. R79 Annex 6).
Distinguished from Automated Driving Systems of SAE levels 3 to 5 (e.g. UN R157 ALKS); DCAS are SAE level 2 according to SAE J3016 / ECE/TRANS/WP29/1140.
Contains an information sharing scheme between approval authorities using DETA.

defined_terms.label: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems
defined_terms.definition: Systems supporting drivers through information, warnings and assistance with lateral and/or longitudinal control, temporarily or on a sustained basis, with the driver remaining responsible.

defined_terms.label: Driver Control Assistance System
defined_terms.definition: A driver-operated vehicle system (subset of ADAS) assisting a human driver in performing vehicle dynamic control via sustained lateral and longitudinal motion-control support.

defined_terms.label: DCAS feature
defined_terms.definition: A specific driver control assistance function of the DCAS (e.g. lane positioning, lane change, other manoeuvre) with its own operating conditions.

defined_terms.label: System boundaries
defined_terms.definition: The conditions within which the DCAS is designed to operate and provide assistance, which constrain its availability and capability.

defined_terms.label: Partial automation
defined_terms.definition: Systems capable of performing only parts of vehicle dynamic control, requiring the driver to perform the remainder and to supervise system operation and environment.

defined_terms.label: Driver assistance
defined_terms.definition: The degraded state in which the DCAS provides only longitudinal or only lateral control.

defined_terms.label: System-initiated manoeuvre
defined_terms.definition: A manoeuvre (e.g. lane change) initiated by the DCAS itself without a prior driver request.

defined_terms.label: Driver-initiated manoeuvre
defined_terms.definition: A manoeuvre initiated by a deliberate driver action and then executed with DCAS assistance.

defined_terms.label: Driver-confirmed manoeuvre
defined_terms.definition: A manoeuvre proposed by the system that is executed only after confirmation by the driver.

defined_terms.label: Lane change
defined_terms.definition: A manoeuvre moving the vehicle from the lane of travel into an adjacent lane, assisted by the DCAS.

defined_terms.label: Driver disengagement
defined_terms.definition: A state in which the driver is not sufficiently engaged in the driving task (e.g. visually or by hands), to be detected and countered by the DCAS.

defined_terms.label: Driver override
defined_terms.definition: Driver input on the controls that takes precedence over DCAS control.

applicability_hints: Any vehicle function that gives sustained combined steering and speed control (e.g. adaptive cruise control combined with lane centering, 'highway assist', 'traffic jam assist') is a DCAS and falls under R171 if approved under it rather than within the R79 ACSF limits.

Approval is of the vehicle type, not of a separate component; suppliers of cameras, radars, steering ECUs, braking actuators or driver-monitoring cameras are affected indirectly through the vehicle approval (Annex 3 safety concept, detection capabilities).
Driver monitoring systems (eye/head tracking, hands-on detection) are relevant via the HMI and driver disengagement requirements in 5.5.
Software updates that change DCAS behaviour are relevant via the R171SWIN and software-update references in Annex 1 and may require extension of the approval.
Systems that offer only longitudinal or only lateral control are not DCAS by themselves; they represent the degraded level 1 state of a DCAS.
Systems that perform the entire driving task (SAE level 3+, e.g. ALKS) are outside R171.
Manufacturers take on in-service monitoring and reporting obligations (section 7), as well as obligations on driver information and marketing.
Simulation tools used to demonstrate compliance must meet the credibility requirements of Annex 5.
